title: introduce-path-aware-premerge-sanity-and-dep-pruner
author: Aisha Raman
description:
Motivation: CI feedback time and noisy dependency churn are recurring pain points. This PR introduces a lightweight "premerge-sanity" lane that boots a minimal lint/test surface for changed paths and a new 'dep-pruner' helper that finds likely-unused devDeps to reduce transitive noise. The goals are: 1) reduce time-to-first-feedback for reviewers by running a fast, path-aware check on PRs; 2) avoid full test/lint runs unless the change touches relevant areas; 3) proactively reduce devDependency bloat and surface candidates for manual review or automatic pruning.

What this PR contains (high-level):
- A new CI lane: .github/workflows/premerge-sanity.yml. This is a fast GitHub Actions job which:
  - uses a small cached container image (node:20-slim-derived) that boots in ~4s on our runners;
  - computes changed paths with git --no-pager diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }};
  - maps paths to test/lint selectors via .ci/path-map.yml;
  - runs eslint (subset config) and the unit-test smoke harness (jest --findRelatedTests) only for the affected packages;
  - publishes an annotation summary (warnings/errors) and exits non-zero if any error is found.
- A path mapping file: .ci/path-map.yml. This YAML maps repo globs to an ordered set of checks (lint, unit-smoke, build). The mapping is intentionally conservative and lives in-tree so teams can opt-in granularly.
- A small utility: tools/path-aware-runner.js (node). Responsible for selecting targets, reducing npm install surface via per-package node_modules caching, and invoking the appropriate commands.
- Dep-pruner: tools/dep-pruner.js. An AST-based analyzer (esbuild parse + a shallow graph walk) that reports devDependencies which appear unused across the workspace. It produces a human-reviewable report and an optional --apply flag that will open a draft PR removing candidates.
- CI integration: premerge-sanity job is enabled by default for PRs against main but resolves quickly for doc-only changes (skips when only markdown). Heavy lanes (integration, E2E, full lint) are only scheduled if path-aware-runner marks the change as broad-impact. There is also a weekly workflow .github/workflows/dep-pruner-weekly.yml that runs dep-pruner, creates a report artifact, and can open draft PRs for maintainers.

Checklist:
- [x] Add path-map and minimal runner
- [x] Add premerge-sanity workflow and cache config
- [x] Add dep-pruner analysis + report mode
- [x] E2E smoke run on a few internal packages (redwood-serving, redwood-api)
- [x] Add docs: docs/ci/premerge-sanity.md and docs/ci/dep-pruner.md
- [x] Tests: unit tests for path mapping logic and dep-pruner heuristics
- [x] Add reviewers and get approvals
commit_summary: 1) add premerge-sanity workflow and path-map template; 2) add tools/path-aware-runner.js and unit tests; 3) add tools/dep-pruner.js with report and apply modes; 4) docs and act preset; 5) CI cache tweaks and workflow guards (doc-skip, small-change fastpath).
review_comments: Jonah Clark (reviewer): Nice approach. Two asks before merge: 1) make the path-map lookup deterministic when multiple globs match (prefer smallest scope); 2) add a way to opt-out per-package via package.json ci.skipPremerge=true. Aisha: addressed in commit 3f8b2c5 — deterministic ordering added and ci.skipPremerge honored.

Marta Silva (reviewer): dep-pruner looks useful, but I'm worried about false-positives for generated code. Can we exclude build output and .generated dirs by default? Aisha: added a default exclude list and configuration in dep-pruner.json; also added a test case for a generated file under packages/docs/.generated/.

Devon Lee (comment): CI cache key looks slightly broad (node-mods-{{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}). Could we squish it to per-package lock hashes to reduce cross-package invalidation? Aisha: updated cache key to include package path when running per-package installs; left monorepo-level cache for weekly jobs.

Unit test failure (CI, initial run): jest unit-tests/tools failed on dep-pruner heuristics — flake due to order of property enumeration. Aisha: fixed by canonicalizing import list in tools/dep-pruner.js and re-ran CI.
Performance note (Jonah): premerge-sanity median runtime on our runners is 18s for small PRs; good improvement.
ci_checks: premerge-sanity: pass (15s), unit-tests: pass, lint-subset: pass, integration-smoke: pass; full-integration: skipped (path-aware). Weekly dep-pruner: queued (success on schedule).
merge_details: Merged by Jonah Clark on 2025-02-20 using squash-merge. Commit message: 'infra: add path-aware premerge sanity lane and dep-pruner utility (ENG-4102, ENG-4227)'. Created follow-up issue ENG-4278 to track expand path-map and automate maintainers review for dep-pruner PRs.
release_notes:
- Add fast 'premerge-sanity' CI lane that runs lint and unit smoke tests only for changed paths to improve PR feedback time.
- Introduce 'dep-pruner' analysis tool to find likely-unused devDependencies and create draft PRs for maintainers.
- Add documentation for configuring path maps and dep-pruner behavior.
runbook:
how to test locally:
1) npm ci && node tools/path-aware-runner.js --preview --changed "packages/runtime/src"
2) node tools/dep-pruner.js --report --out dep-pruner-report.json
3) act --workflow premerge-sanity.yml to emulate the GitHub Action locally (we have a small act preset in .github/act-config.yml)
Links: Linear: ENG-4102 (path-aware premerge) | ENG-4227 (dep-pruner prototype). Related: RFC: rfc/ci-path-aware.md. Security considerations: dep-pruner only inspects sources and package.json devDeps; it never touches production dependencies and when run with --apply it creates draft PRs rather than committing directly. Migration notes: teams that rely on our existing full-lint feedback should add their package globs to .ci/path-map.yml to ensure the minimal checks include their packages. This PR intentionally errs on the conservative side and preserves full-lint for changes flagged as broad-impact.
